content.rendered:
It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery. The believer is not trying to become free. The believer has been set free. The work now is to stand in it.

The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, July 7, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm, then, and do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery.”
Galatians 5:1 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul writes Galatians to churches that were drifting back into law-based religion. They had received the gospel of grace, experienced the freedom that comes from being justified by faith in Christ, and then started listening to teachers who told them they needed to add the works of the law to keep their standing with God. Paul is furious in this letter, not at the believers themselves, but at the false teachers who were robbing them of the freedom Christ had purchased for them. Galatians 5:1 is the climax of his argument. Christ has set you free. Stand in it.

The phrase Paul uses is dense in the Greek. It can be translated literally as “for freedom Christ has freed us.” The repetition is deliberate. Freedom is not a side benefit of the gospel. Freedom is the purpose of the gospel. The cross is not just about getting forgiven and trying harder. The cross is about a fundamental change of status. The believer was a slave. The believer is now free. The work of Christ on the cross was specifically designed to produce that outcome.

And the freedom Paul names is comprehensive. Freedom from the law as a system of earning standing with God. Freedom from the power of sin in daily life. Freedom from the fear of death. Freedom from the accusations of the enemy. Freedom from the performance treadmill of religion. Freedom from the slavery of trying to earn what has already been given. Every form of bondage the believer was under before Christ has been broken by Christ.

And then Paul gives the practical instruction. Stand firm. Do not let yourselves be burdened again by a yoke of slavery. The danger for the Galatian believers was not that they would commit grand sins. The danger was that they would let well-meaning religious teachers put them back into a system the cross had already freed them from. The same danger exists for believers today. Religious culture is full of yokes ready to be placed on the shoulders of free believers. Performance yokes. Legalism yokes. Comparison yokes. Condemnation yokes. The work of the believer is not to put them on. It is to stand firm in the freedom Christ purchased.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is liberating. You are free in Christ. Not pursuing freedom. Free. The work today is not to earn the freedom. It is to refuse the yokes that try to lock it away from you again. Stand firm. Walk free. This is who you are in Christ.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I am free in Christ. The freedom is already mine, purchased at the cross by the precious blood of Jesus. I am not a slave to sin. I am not a slave to fear. I am not a slave to the law as a means of earning standing with You. I refuse every yoke of slavery that tries to settle back on my shoulders. I stand firm in the freedom Christ has secured for me. I walk free today, light, unburdened, and at home in the liberty of the gospel. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am free in Christ. The freedom is mine. I stand firm in it. I refuse every yoke of slavery the enemy tries to lay on me. I walk free today.
